plan.title: Quote private pickups at the ordinary fee level
plan.from_topics: Unquoted requests (proposal 2) + Small leaks (proposal 2): same idea, merged
plan.why: Largest block the bot declines: 72.4 requests a week, EUR 5,800 of list price. The only earlier tests priced the class out (costPrivate 0.3-0.6, privateFee 1.2-1.5): quotes went out at 1.71 x list against 1.54, so 19-20% were won against 40%, and the gigs booked in a median 4-6 minutes at 1.08 x typical, so the fee surcharge bought nothing. The 6-7 orders a week that were won made EUR 35-39 each and were 1.8-2.9% late. The switch exists and nothing else has to move: decline at desk.ts line 886, costPrivate in the cost at line 923, privateFee in schedule() at line 1313.
plan.test: Config only, base C:\Users\trevo\spread\bot\sweeps\cand5.json. Four variants: (a) quotePrivatePickup true (privateFee 1 and costPrivate 0.15 are already cand5's values, so only the switch moves); (b) the same with privateFee 1.1; (c) cand5 with minAwake 360 and (d) the same with quotePrivatePickup true. Pair (c)/(d) isolates slots 6+ waking hours away, the only group ever tested; (a) against it shows the group with a slot 4-5 waking hours away (29.7 requests a week) that cand5's minAwake 240 lets through for the first time. Seeds: 40 usual against tag sa-awk240-cap140-pow15-st16, then h1-h80 against sa-awk240-cap140-pow15-st16-u (lanesFile lanes-usual.json as in sau.json). Read private-pickup orders on their own: count won, win share, quote multiple, fee over lane value, minutes to booking, no_show events, late share split by waking hours from the reply to the slot's end (4-5 h / 6+ h) and by distance (under / over 150 km); then weekly margin, on-time share and the worst week. Stop if the class is more than about 8% late or the worst week falls below the base's.
plan.doubts: Both analysts claimed 150-200; I keep 90 with a range of about -100 to +250. The class margin was measured (EUR 240 a week) but the whole week was flat in both old arms (-62 +-111, -1 +-105), so other orders may have paid for it, and the notes of 14 Nov list private quoting as 'no gain' at the old pricing. The expected 11-13 orders a week at ordinary pricing is an extrapolation. On cand5 the switch also opens slots only 4-5 waking hours away, never quoted before: the mean lane is 228 km, ordinary orders in that band are 12-37% late from 150 km up, and a missed private slot never extends (no_show, next business day), so a miss is a certain late order. With so little lead the calm ramp has almost no room (it ends 200 minutes before the last pickup), so the fee will rise fast, which is known to lose money. The late model and the start model in cand5 have no privPu term (checked), so the quote prices no extra risk. If the 4-5 hour group turns out bad, the fix is a one-line gate at desk.ts line 910 (own minAwake of 360 for private pickups).

plan.title: Switch the fitted offer model on
plan.why: cand5 leaves offerModel null, so offers go by the point score: 58% of them go to drivers who never viewed the order, live more than 30 km from the delivery and have not worked today, and return 1 accept in 3,760, while they use up the three offers a driver may get a day (2,501 of 3,003 offered driver-days hit that limit). Offers to a driver who viewed the order in the last 30 minutes are taken 1.1-1.6% of the time against 0.16%, yet only 393 a week are sent. The model that spends offers on those drivers is already in the code (sendModelOffers, desk.ts lines 1540-1598) and scored +146 +-108 with 26.7 accepts a week against 17.9 in its only test. On-time share was unchanged there.
plan.test: Config only, base cand5: offerModel = the object under "o2-m004" in C:\Users\trevo\spread\bot\sweeps\o2.json (checked: one -5.992, deAt 1.637, de30 1.434, de80 0.6, pu30 -0.284, here -0.184, worked 0.958, seen 0.101, long -1.181, fee -1.442, today -0.437, view30 2.303, view120 1.991, view600 1.255, viewOld -0.559, hour -1.593, evening -0.442, lnDone 0.387); offerMin stays at its default 0.004. The EUR 330 for offers was measured on s7-k115; an accepted offer saves the later raise, and cand5's lower, slower ramp (cap 1.4) leaves less to save, so both the 330 and this gain are probably smaller on cand5. The model was fitted with the fee over the request's noisy typical fee, and desk.ts line 1561 still divides by referenceFeeCents, so its fee term is noisy on a lane-anchored config. offerMin 0.002 was already in the o2 sweep; look at that result before spending a run on 0.003. An effect of this size cannot be proven by weekly margin on 120 worlds; the accept count and the fee at booking are the readable signs.

plan.title: Give the opening-fee model the day the car is ready
plan.why: The start model has no feature for how many days ahead the car is ready, and it is wrong along exactly that axis on 34,062 orders: ready today it says 0.68 booked at the opening fee, actual 0.58; ready tomorrow 0.75 against 0.82; in 2 days 0.78 against 0.46; in 3+ days 0.79 against 0.30. A residual fit holds out of sample both ways (log loss 0.625 to 0.560 and 0.612 to 0.551, coefficients within 0.1). It matches the handbook's rule that a driver books a later day only when they know they will work it. This is the largest measured error in the fee path, and the same model also sets each quote's cost (costStart 1).
plan.test: Step 1, config only: cand5 with startModel.lnOLane = -0.855 added (the feature exists, desk.ts line 758; cand5's startModel has no such key). Step 2, code in C:\Users\trevo\spread\bot\desk.ts features() (lines 719-764): rdy0 = 1 when floor(earliest/DAY) equals floor(request.respondBy/DAY) and that day is Mon-Thu; rdy2 = 1 when the difference is 2; rdy3 = 1 when it is 3 or more; deMid = 1 when roster.near(de, 30) is 10 to 149. Arm C: full refit with tools/startfit.py including the new features. In every arm reset costStartMean (now 0.95) to the new mean of expect over saved quotes. 40 usual seeds and h1-h80. Read by ready-day group: opening fee over lane, share booked at opening, final fee over lane, late share, and the number of quotes won.
plan.doubts: Claimed 150, from 240 on the model's own arithmetic. That arithmetic prices a miss at the configured 1.2 x lane, while missed orders really book at 1.00 (ready tomorrow) and 0.92-0.94 (2+ days). For cars ready in 2+ days the proposal opens 0.09-0.14 higher, yet their post-day bookings at 0.75-0.81 x lane are the cheapest of all, so the direction for that group (126 of the 240) may be wrong; arm B is there to settle it. Quote side: expect uses the plain startFallback 1.2, so cars ready in 2+ days would be costed roughly 0.15-0.2 lane values higher while their real final fee is only 0.03-0.08 above what the model implied; those quotes would lose wins. Without re-centring costStartMean the test is also a hidden change of price level, which the feeK runs show is worth +-100 by itself. The Friday definition is not stated: counted in calendar days, a Friday post for a car ready Monday gets rdy3 (-2.73); it must match the fit script (scratch/feepath/a5.py on the server) exactly or most Friday orders open far too high. About 10 more ready-tomorrow orders a week go onto the ramp: roughly +0.3 late orders a week.

plan.title: After a change of destination, anchor the fee on the new lane
plan.from_topics: Late orders (proposal 1) + Small leaks (proposal 1): same bug found twice, merged
plan.why: Verified in the code: onChanged() (desk.ts line 1019) stores the new order but never touches ord.request, and schedule() takes its reference from refOf(ord.request, ...) at line 1314; ord.shownFee also holds the opening at the old level. So lane anchoring has a hole: both analysts measured reposts opening at 0.87-0.89 x the OLD lane in every group. Nearer place (about 1 order a week): booked at 2.4-3.4 x the new lane value, EUR 52-60 a week overpaid. Farther place (0.8 a week): nobody books until the urgent ramp, 69% late, margin EUR -47 an order; 57 of the 74 orders that were never delivered or cost the whole price had such a change. It is the one proposal with a certain mechanism, and it improves the on-time share.
plan.test: Code in C:\Users\trevo\spread\bot\desk.ts behind a new Config flag changeRef (default false). Add refScale (start 1) to Ord (type near line 349, set near line 999). In onChanged, before the open gigs are withdrawn: for a one-leg order whose pickup or delivery placeId differs from ord.request.legs[0], scale = lanes[newPickup>newDelivery] / lanes[requestPickup>requestDelivery] from lanesOf(cfg.lanesFile) (ratio of roadMinutes when a lane is missing; 1 for two legs); multiply ord.shownFee by scale / ord.refScale, set ord.refScale = scale and ord.climb = null. In schedule() line 1314 multiply ref by ord.refScale (same factor for the offer model's fee at line 1561). Run the 40 usual seeds against sa-awk240-cap140-pow15-st16 and judge on the affected orders, not the weekly mean: changed orders that had no driver (about 1.9 a week): fee paid over the NEW lane value where the place is nearer (target 0.9-1.0 instead of 2.4-3.4), late share where it is farther (target under 25% instead of 69%), number never delivered. Weekly margin only as a check that nothing else moved.
plan.doubts: Both analysts say 70. The mechanism is certain; the size rests on 75-118 orders. A gig posted again does not notify drivers a second time (a driver hears of each order once), so the nearer-place gig may sit longer or need more than 0.9 x the new lane. The farther-place half is about neutral in cash (EUR 11 more fees against EUR 22-34 fewer refunds); its value is on-time share and dealer trust, about 0.5 fewer late orders a week. live.ts rebuilds its books from the world on every start, so refScale has to be recomputed there (order's places against the request's) or the fix is lost after a restart in the final. The effect is far below weekly noise, so it can only be accepted on the per-order evidence.

plan.title: Narrower learning scale: market.scale 0.065 and 0.06
plan.why: Every paired 40-week comparison of a narrower scale on older configs came out positive (+26 to +379), and no s7/s8/s9/sa tag varied it; cand5 still runs 0.07. The analyst's reading is that the benefit is learning speed: regret is highest at 08-10 h and on the morning after the price war, when the belief lags. It costs nothing to run.
plan.test: Config only, base cand5 (market.scale 0.07): market.scale 0.065 and 0.06, all else equal. 40 usual seeds paired, then h1-h80. Read margin, orders won a week, on-time share and the lowest week. The unattended tuner's market.scale knob steps by 0.01, so 0.06 may already come out of a tuner round; read that instead of running it twice.
plan.doubts: Claimed 40. Only one of the five older tests is significant, and that one is on a much older model; 0.07 was itself chosen by replay log loss (mk2). In the old tests the narrower scale won 4-10 more orders a week with on-time 0.2-0.3 points lower and a worst week of 90.3%, right at the 90% ranking floor: for a final that picks the ten best ranked teams that tail matters more than EUR 30. It also steepens a pricing curve that the same analyst measured as already too steep (slope 0.865), so it pulls against item 12.

plan.title: Take trade-ins as one gig, costed at what drivers charged, with the gig opening near that fee
plan.from_topics: Unquoted requests (proposal 4) + Small leaks (proposal 3): merged into one test with arms
plan.why: 19.7 requests a week declined with a list price 1.72 x the typical fee, far richer than a single car. In the 16-week tests the class made EUR 230-330 a week gross at EUR 45-55 an order. Two things were wrong in those runs and both are settable: the quote's cost (feeK + 0.2) sat below the fee actually paid (1.4-1.5 x typical), and the gig opened at 0.90 x and had to climb the whole ramp, which is where the 15-19% late share comes from. schedule() line 1313 applies privateFee to any order with a private pickup; while quotePrivatePickup is off that reaches trade-in gigs only.
plan.test: Config only, base cand5 with quotePrivatePickup false: quoteTradeIns true, tradeSlot 0 (already the default; never run without it), tradeLate 0.2, costTrade 0.5, with arms privateFee 1 (repeats tr2-s0-cost5 on the current base), 1.25 and 1.4; optional fourth arm costTrade 0.7 with privateFee 1.25. 40 usual seeds. Read trade-in orders on their own: count, win share (aim 38-45%), late share, opening fee and fee paid over typical (check in the journal that the gig really opens at about 0.9 x privateFee; that relies on the old car's pickup being flagged as a private address), minutes to booking, margin an order. Drop the idea if the class stays above about 8-10% late. If item 1 is adopted the privateFee arms collide with it: add a separate setting (e.g. tradeFee) at desk.ts line 1313 for two-leg orders.
plan.doubts: Both analysts say 100. All evidence is 16 weeks on an old base and the three whole-week results are -192 +-253, +88 +-184 and +92 +-175: zero within noise. Even with tradeSlot 0 the class was 15-19% late, about 0.8 more late orders a week (-0.2 points); that a higher opening cures it is inferred from the fee path, not measured. The two analysts' numbers do not agree with the first one's remedy: costTrade 0.5 already gave a 38% win share at 1.53 x list, so costTrade 0.6-0.8 would overshoot. Trade-ins are not lane-anchored (refOf returns the request's own number for two legs), and 8.5 of the 19.7 cannot run as one gig at all.

plan.title: Let offers go out for next-day pickups (replace the 20-hour cut-off)
plan.why: Verified: both offer routines skip any gig whose pickup opens more than 20 hours ahead (desk.ts lines 1554 and 1614), so an order won in the morning for tomorrow morning gets no offer during the minutes when most drivers look at it. Just inside the limit offers are taken more often, not less (0.40% at 14-20 h against 0.22% for cars ready now), offers in an order's first 30 minutes are taken 0.59-0.66% against 0.13-0.27% later, and 30% of the drivers who viewed low and booked higher first looked while the pickup was more than 20 h away. The change is one number.
plan.test: Code in C:\Users\trevo\spread\bot\desk.ts: new Config offerAhead (hours, default 20) in place of the literal 20 at lines 1554 (sendModelOffers) and 1614 (sendOffers). Test 30 and 44, each with the offer model of item 2 on and with it off. 40 usual seeds. The offer model has no term for how far ahead the pickup is (only 'today'). Not additive with items 2 and 13.

plan.title: Hold the calm ramp while nobody books: nights above the lane value, and the weekend for Monday orders
plan.from_topics: Fee path (proposals 2 and 3): same mechanism and same code place, merged
plan.why: 34% of orders miss their opening fee and pay EUR 1,920 a week above it; 46% of those bookings come between 00:00 and 09:00. 32% of all fee climb is scheduled at 18:00-21:00, when the booking chance per open order-hour is 0.06-0.07 against 0.19-0.27 at 06-08 h, and a raise sends no notification. For orders due the next day the share booked by 09:00 does not rise with the fee above the lane value (79% at 0.98, 85% at 1.11, 82% at 1.21). Weekend: awakeMinutes/afterAwake (desk.ts lines 422-447) count Saturday afternoon and Sunday as waking hours, so the fee climbs while under 2% an hour book, and the Monday-morning cohort pays 1.46 x lane. It fits what is known: paying sooner than drivers decide loses money.
plan.test: Code in C:\Users\trevo\spread\bot\desk.ts schedule(), the calm-ramp loop at line 1386 only (not the urgent, late or drop-climb branches). New Config: nightCap number | null (null), nightFrom 18, nightTo 9, weekendHold boolean (false). A ramp step whose fee is above ref x nightCap and whose minute falls in [nightFrom, 24:00) or [00:00, nightTo) moves to the next nightTo o'clock, unless that is later than lastPickupAt - rampLead (then it stays). With weekendHold a step on Saturday from 15:00 or on Sunday moves to Monday 07:00 under the same guard. Arms on cand5: nightCap 1.0, 1.1 and 0; nightTo 9 and 7; weekendHold alone; nightCap 1.0 with weekendHold. 40 usual seeds and h1-h80. Read: for orders open at 23:00 with the last pickup next day, the fee over lane at first booking and the share booked by 09:00; for Friday orders due Monday, the fee paid by the Monday 00-09 cohort and the share booked after Monday 09:00; evening bookings 18-21 h; on-time share.
plan.doubts: Claimed 120 + 40. The flat response above the lane value is observational: the dearer orders are the older, harder ones, and the coefficient is -3.5 +-1.9. It was measured on the cap-1.6 ramp; cand5's cap 1.4 with rampPow 1.5 already keeps the overnight fee lower, and the analyst expects about half there. A lower evening fee can only lose evening bookings; they were assumed unchanged. The hold ends with several steps at once at 09:00, a jump in the middle of the best booking hours, so nightTo 7 against 9 is a real question. Whole-ramp compressions (rampAwake 600/900) lost EUR 1,400-2,200, so the guard on lastPickupAt - rampLead must be tested with early last pickups. Weekend part: only 2.5 orders a week; Monday bookers after 09:00 end late 64% of the time, so one in ten slipping costs about +0.15 late orders a week. The two holds overlap; do not add their gains.

plan.title: Close the gig at the last on-time pickup and repost it late at once
plan.why: By the rules, once no driver can still be on time a stop without its own window runs to the end of the world, so the urgent gig (1.6-2.5 x) becomes bookable for any later day. 1.45 orders a week are booked in the 10-60 minutes before the desk notices (round() acts at lastPickupAt + 5, line 1496), 196 of 348 within six minutes, at 1.67 x lane; all end late anyway, a median 17.8 h later. Orders that reach the late repost book at 1.15-1.17 x with the same lateness. Fees paid in the gap above 1.15 x: EUR 49.7 a week.
plan.test: Code in C:\Users\trevo\spread\bot\desk.ts behind a flag lateCut. In plan(), on-time branch (lines 1195-1200), for dealer pickups only: give the pickup stop its own window from max(earliest, leg.pickup.window.from) to ord.order.lastPickupAt (the world's value, not the desk's estimate); the world then expires the gig in the minute after. In onExpired (line 1436): when now >= ord.order.lastPickupAt set ord.late = true and ord.lateSince = now and post the late gig in the same call (forced late plan, so schedule() takes lateStart 1.15), not at the next round. 40 usual seeds. Read: bookings between the last on-time pickup and the late repost (now 1.45 a week, should be none), fees on late orders, refund tiers, counts of driver_late and no_show events, on-time share (must not move).
plan.doubts: Claimed 35 (range 25-45). The saved files cannot show whether the drivers who took 1.67 x would take 1.15 x; half of reposted late gigs book within the hour. The window also binds a driver who has already booked: one who slips past it reports driver_late at an open dealer site (still comes) but no_show otherwise, for instance when the last pickup is the site's closing time, and the gig then reopens; the 2.2 orders a week that are booked and collected late could land in a worse refund tier. desk.ts has no driver_late handler. It must fit with windows that already exist (the buffered delivery window, note-pinned plans; postLeg deletes ended windows at line 1232), and where the desk's own lastPickup() still sees an on-time pickup the repost has to be forced late.

proposals.confidence: Medium-low: the overpayment is measured (EUR 79 a week above 0.95 x the new lane for ratio under 0.5), but release has never been used by this desk, so the fee base and the re-booking speed are untested.
proposals.ontime_risk: Small if limited to pickups more than a day away (short trips, re-booked on a fresh ramp); real if applied with under 12 h left. About 0.6-1.2 orders a week affected.

proposals.title: dropSafe 240 instead of 360: reopen a dropped gig from the booked fee also with 4 to 6 hours left
proposals.evidence: All 16,703 drops before the last on-time pickup in 240 weeks (69.6 a week), by minutes left. Just under the threshold (300-360 min, n=257, reopened at 1.1 x the schedule's fee): rebooked at 1.47 x lane, EUR 22.1 more than the dropped booking, order late 8.6%. Just above (360-420 min, n=236, reopened at 1.1 x the booked fee): rebooked at 1.22 x lane, EUR 11.4 more, order late 10.6%. Pooled neighbours: 240-360 min (n=450) late 8.3%, EUR 23.2 extra; 360-480 min (n=575) late 8.2%, EUR 10.9 extra. So the dearer reopening costs about EUR 12 a drop and buys no on-time share in this band. Below 240 min lateness climbs (16% at 180-240, 29% at 120-180), so the dearer way should stay there.
proposals.mechanism: With 4 to 6 hours left the binding limit is which drivers can still reach the pickup, not the fee: a reopening at 1.1 x the booked fee finds the same drivers as one at 1.1 x the ramp's fee, and the ramp still climbs to its cap before the urgent phase.
proposals.test: Config only: dropSafe: 240 (all else as s7-k115), 40 usual seeds; a second arm dropSafe: 180. Compare fees after drops with 240-360 minutes left and the on-time share of those orders.
proposals.confidence: Medium: a clean jump in the rebooked fee at the 360-minute threshold with equal lateness on both sides, but n is about 250 a side and 1.9 drops a week are affected.
proposals.ontime_risk: Low for 240 (late share equal on both sides of the present threshold); 180 adds a band where 16% already end late, so watch it.

proposals.title: Give a late repost a delivery window to the next refund step instead of leaving it open-ended
proposals.evidence: 240 weeks, late orders without a driver at the last on-time pickup. The late gig is posted without windows (plan(), 'the stops run to the end of the world'), so the driver picks the day. Monday-Thursday: 216 orders in the 50% tier (EUR 47 a week refunded); 82 of them were booked within 14 h of the last on-time pickup (37 within 3 h) and still delivered more than 24 h late; 98 were collected 28-48 h after it. Friday: 492 late (2.05 a week, EUR 129 a week); where both sites are open on Saturday (362), 188 were delivered on Saturday (25%) and 170 on Monday or later (50%, EUR 76 a week); 75 of those 170 were booked within 3 h of the last on-time pickup. Where only the delivery site opens on Saturday, all 112 went to 50%. Step from 25% to 50%: about EUR 35 an order (mean price EUR 141).
proposals.mechanism: Refund steps are at deadline + 24 h and + 2 business days. A driver who books a windowless late gig takes whichever day suits them; a delivery window ending at the next step (Saturday closing for a Friday deadline) makes the booking land inside the cheaper tier or leaves the gig for a driver who can.
proposals.test: Code change in desk.ts plan(), late branch (about line 1187), behind a flag (e.g. lateTier: boolean): set deliveryStop.window.to = min(deadline + 1440, that day's closing of the delivery site, Saturday hours included) while now + drive + 30 still fits and the pickup site is open before then; when that passes, post open-ended as now (next step: + 2 business days). Keep lateStart 1.15 and the present late ramp. Compare the tier mix of late orders and the fees paid on them on the 40 usual seeds.
proposals.confidence: Low-medium: the tier slips are counted, but the saved files cannot show whether another driver takes the windowed gig at a similar fee; the 157 early bookers may simply not work the next day.
proposals.ontime_risk: None: it only touches orders that are already late. Risk is a slower booking of the late gig while the window is on; the fallback to open-ended limits it.

found.nothing_found:
Causes of the 2,312 late orders (9.6 a week): never booked before the last on-time pickup 852 (3.55 a week, EUR 230 a week refunded, mean quote-time late chance 0.129); booked, dropped and not rebooked in time 692 (2.88 a week, EUR 129, 0.059); driver held the gig but collected late 528 (2.2 a week, EUR 74, 0.068); collected on time, delivered late 240 (1.0 a week, EUR 37, 0.081).

Lines that gave no rule:
1. A higher or earlier urgent fee. Of the 852 never-booked orders, 806 had 50+ distinct viewers before the last on-time pickup, the fee stood at 1.2-1.6 x lane eight hours before it for two thirds, at 2-2.5 x at the end, with 134 direct offers each. Once the windows fell away, 65% of unbooked late orders booked within 3 h at 1.15-1.6 x. The limit in the last hours is drivers who can make the window, not the fee. Saved files cannot say what a higher fee the day before would have done.
2. Not quoting by late chance. No band of the quote-time chance loses money after refunds: 0.25-0.35 earns EUR 101 an order (n=450), 0.5+ EUR 141 (n=95). The worst-predicted group, same-day 250-400 km with under 7 waking hours to the last pickup (28.6% late against 8.1% predicted, n=161), still earns EUR 44.6 an order. Trust loss is not in these margins.
3. Quote-time late chance: AUC 0.79 overall; by cause 0.88 never booked, 0.72 dropped, 0.73 collected late, 0.76 delivered late. Calibrated up to 0.12 (0.096 predicted, 0.077 actual), too high above: 0.21 predicted vs 0.16, 0.29 vs 0.19, 0.41 vs 0.25, 0.65 vs 0.31 (761 orders from 0.25 up, nearly all 400+ km). A shrink above 0.18 would cheapen long-haul quotes; I did not size it because it needs the win model.
4. Midnight drops. A third of drops come at 00:01-00:20 (5,654; 23.6 a week). With 10-16 h left they end late 20-25% of the time (400+ km: 25.3%, n=525), but a dearer reopening for them does not pay on these numbers: about EUR 40 more per drop against an expected late cost of about EUR 29.
5. Drivers who hold the gig and collect late: 128 of 528 follow a change of destination that moved the last pickup earlier (the world re-routes, extra driving is cheap, nothing to do); the other 366 booked mostly more than a day ahead and came 0-60 minutes late in half the cases. The saved event logs hold no driver_late event (14 weeks checked) and desk.ts has no handler for it, so a release-the-late-driver rule cannot be judged from saved files.
6. Snow and the delivery buffer. Drives in snow take 25% longer at the median (40% at p90); orders collected 30-120 minutes before the last pickup end late 28.8% in snow against 0.6% without. But only 78 such late deliveries in 240 weeks (EUR 12 a week refunded), so a snow buffer is worth under EUR 20 a week. One detail: a delivery a few minutes after a 20:00 closing costs 25%, not 10% (73 of 73 cases).
7. A lower late fee than 1.15: 479 late orders booked at exactly 1.15 x within 0.5-3 h, which hints that some would take less, but there is no variation in the saved files to measure it.

Caveat: the 240 weeks are five near-identical configs on 120 distinct worlds, so counts per week are sound but the weeks are not independent. The 270 MB timeline file /mnt/data/trevor/spread/scratch/late/tl_s7-k115.pkl is left in place for re-checks; delete it when done.

found.topic: Fee path of orders that do not book at their opening fee, and when to post or raise (80 saved weeks: s7-k115 on the 40 usual seeds plus s8-l35-u on h1..h40; 34,062 orders posted on the calm ramp)

proposals.title: Give the opening-fee model the day the car is ready (plus mid-density delivery towns, a waiting order on the same lane, and a Friday correction)
proposals.evidence: 80 weeks, 34,062 orders. Overall the start model says 0.70 booked at opening, actual 0.66. The error sits along an axis the model has no feature for, the days from the post to the day the car is ready (Mon-Thu posts): ready today 120.8 orders/wk, model 0.68, actual 0.58; ready tomorrow 205.1/wk, model 0.75, actual 0.82; ready in 2 days 22.7/wk, model 0.78, actual 0.46; ready in 3+ days 16.9/wk, model 0.79, actual 0.30. Also delivery towns with 10-149 drivers within 30 km (203/wk): model 0.69-0.72, actual 0.58-0.65; orders with another own order waiting on the same lane (32/wk): model 0.67, actual 0.51. A residual fit with the model's own output as offset (fee slope untouched) gives: one +0.81, rdy0 (ready on the post day, Mon-Thu) -0.94, rdy2 -1.96, rdy3 (3+ days) -2.73, deMid (10-149 drivers near delivery) -0.60, lnOLane -0.855, postFri -0.55 on top of the present -4.03; standard errors 0.03-0.06. Out of sample both ways (fit on usual 40, scored on fresh 40, and the reverse) log loss falls from 0.625 to 0.560 and from 0.612 to 0.551, with coefficients within 0.1 of each other. Re-choosing each opening fee with the corrected chance and the configured fallback gives 240 EUR/wk on the model's own arithmetic (ready today +34, tomorrow +80 with openings 0.03 lower, 2 days +55 with openings 0.09 higher, 3+ days +71 with openings 0.14 higher). The same model also sets the fee in each quote's cost (costStart 1): final fee over lane value is 0.99 for ready today, 0.88 for tomorrow, 0.90 and 0.93 for 2 and 3+ days, against 0.98, 0.91, 0.87, 0.85 implied by the model.
proposals.mechanism: Drivers book a later day only when they know they will work it. In the data that is a gradient, not a gate: 93% of first bookings for a car ready tomorrow come on the post day, 64% for ready in 2 days, 42% for 3 days, 26% for 4 days. The model was fitted without this, so it opens cars ready tomorrow too high and cars ready in 2+ days too low; the latter then sit, climb, and book next morning at 0.91 x lane (70% of those bookers had viewed the gig the day before), which also teaches viewers that these fees rise.
proposals.test: Code change in bot/desk.ts, features() (about lines 716-760): add rdy0 = 1 when floor(earliest/DAY) equals floor(request.respondBy/DAY) and that day is Mon-Thu, rdy2 = 1 when the difference is 2, rdy3 = 1 when it is 3 or more, deMid = 1 when the delivery town has 10 to 149 drivers within 30 km. Then in startModel add keys rdy0 -0.94, rdy2 -1.96, rdy3 -2.73, deMid -0.60, lnOLane -0.855 (lnOLane is already in feat, so that key alone is a config-only test), raise one by +0.81 and move postFri from -4.0291 to -4.58. Run on the usual 40 and h1-h80 against the base. Second variant: a full refit with tools/startfit.py including the new features. Scripts and the fitted numbers: /mnt/data/trevor/spread/scratch/feepath/a5.py.
proposals.confidence: Medium-high that the model is wrong along this axis (stable out of sample, 80 weeks). Medium on the size: the 240 assumes a miss costs the configured fallback of 1.2, while measured first bookings after a miss are 1.00 x lane for ready tomorrow and 0.92-0.94 for 2+ days, so the split between groups will differ.
proposals.ontime_risk: Low. Cars ready today and in 2+ days open higher and book sooner. Cars ready tomorrow open about 0.03 lower, which puts roughly 10 more orders a week on the ramp; those end late 5.7% of the time against 2.3% overall, about +0.3 late orders a week (0.07 points).

proposals.title: Night hold on the calm ramp: no raise above the lane value between 18:00 and 09:00
proposals.evidence: 144 orders/wk (34%) do not book at opening and pay 1,920 EUR/wk above their opening fees at first booking. 46% of those bookings come between 00:00 and 09:00 and carry about 1,000 EUR of the 1,920. Booking chance per open order-hour (Mon-Thu posts): 06h 0.19, 07h 0.27, 08h 0.19, daytime 0.09-0.13, 18-21h 0.06-0.07, 22h-05h 0.003-0.05. Yet 32% of all fee climb (7.1 of 22.2 lane values/wk, about 460 EUR on open orders) is scheduled at 18:00-21:00, and another 10% at 07:00-09:00 in the middle of the morning burst. Next-morning bookers (32.9/wk, 55-71% of them seeing the gig for the first time) paid 308 EUR/wk more than the fee shown at 18:00 the evening before. For orders whose last on-time pickup is the next day and that are open at 23:00, the share booked by 09:00 does not rise with the fee: 79% at 0.98 x lane (2.8/wk), 85% at 1.11 (14.3/wk), 82% at 1.21 (6.4/wk); logistic coefficient on the climb -3.5 +-1.9 with age, viewers, opening fee and model chance as controls. The 22 orders/wk sitting above 1.0 that night carry about 2.7 lane values (175 EUR/wk) above 1.0 into the morning. For orders with two or more days left the morning share does rise with the fee (44% at 0.83, 64% at 0.95, 70% at 1.10; coefficient 8.5 +-1.4), so the hold should not apply below the lane value. Past sweeps point the same way: in sweep sa (usual 40) feeCap 1.4 with rampPow 1.5 and feeSteps 16 scored +457 over its base, while compressing the ramp globally (rampAwake 600/900) lost 1,400-2,200.
proposals.mechanism: Each morning a new set of drivers decides to work and books what suits them at the fee then in the app; a raise sends no notification, so evening raises reach few drivers and are mostly paid to the morning cohort, which for an order due that day books at about the lane value as readily as at 1.2 times it. Holding the fee overnight lets that cohort look at the lower fee first; at 09:00 the schedule jumps back onto its present path, so daytime speed and the time the cap is reached do not change.
proposals.test: Code change in bot/desk.ts, schedule(), the calm-ramp loop at about line 1383 (not the urgent, late or drop-climb branches): new Config nightCap: number | null (default null), nightFrom: 18, nightTo: 9. For each ramp step, if its fee is above ref * nightCap and its minute falls in [nightFrom, 24:00) or [00:00, nightTo), move it to the next nightTo o'clock, unless that is later than lastPickupAt - rampLead (then leave it). Variants: nightCap 1.0, 1.1 and 0 (hold every evening step); nightTo 9 and 7. Run on the present base and on the sa-awk240-cap140-pow15-st16 settings, where the overnight fee is already lower and the gain will be smaller.
proposals.confidence: Low to medium. The timing facts are solid (80 weeks); the flat response above the lane value is observational and the dearer orders are the older, harder ones. Upper bound about 175-300 EUR/wk if the same drivers book at the held fee; perhaps half that on the cap-1.4 convex ramp.
proposals.ontime_risk: Low to moderate. The affected orders are on their last morning. Their fee returns to the present path at 09:00 with the ramp end unchanged. If the hold cuts morning bookings from 82% to 79%, about 0.7 more orders a week face the last-morning ramp, where 5-11% end late: under 0.1 late orders a week. The guard on lastPickupAt - rampLead keeps early last pickups out.

proposals.title: Weekend hold for Friday orders due Monday: no raise from Saturday 15:00 to Monday 07:00
proposals.evidence: Friday posts with the last pickup on Monday: 53.6/wk. 19.5/wk book on Friday at the opening fee, 24/wk on Saturday before 09:00 (18.7 of them above opening at 0.96 x lane), 5.6/wk on Saturday 09:00-15:00. After Saturday 15:00 3.4 orders/wk are still open; only 0.77/wk book from then until Sunday midnight (chance under 0.02 an hour), while the fee climbs 0.96 lane values/wk, about +0.28 per open order. The Monday 00:00-09:00 cohort (2.1/wk, all picked up Monday, none late, 70% had viewed the gig earlier) then pays 1.46 x lane: 290 EUR/wk against 220 at the fee of Saturday 15:00 and 177 at opening.
proposals.mechanism: Sunday every site is closed and almost nobody books; drivers who work Monday decide on Monday morning and take the fee they find. The ramp counts Saturday afternoon and Sunday as waking hours, so it raises the fee for a cohort that could not have booked earlier.
proposals.test: Same code place as the night hold (bot/desk.ts, schedule(), calm-ramp loop near line 1383): new Config weekendHold: boolean (default false). A ramp step whose minute falls on Saturday from 15:00 or on Sunday moves to Monday 07:00, unless that is later than lastPickupAt - rampLead. Test alone and together with nightCap.
proposals.confidence: Medium on the measurement, low on the size: the upper bound is about 70 EUR/wk and only 2.5 orders a week are affected.
proposals.ontime_risk: Low in total but concentrated: all affected orders are due Monday. Monday bookers after 09:00 end late 64% of the time, so if the lower fee moves one in ten early-Monday bookings past 09:00 that is about +0.15 late orders a week (0.03 points).

proposals.title: Opening-fee fallback by weekday in line with what a miss costs: lower on Monday, higher on Thursday
proposals.evidence: An order that misses its opening fee books first at these multiples of the lane value, by post day (80 weeks): Mon 1.00, Tue 1.05, Wed 1.05, Thu 1.08, Fri 1.04. Excess over the opening fee per missed order: Mon 11.5 EUR, Tue 12.3, Wed 13.4, Thu 17.3, Fri 12.5. Late share of missed orders: Mon 3.7%, Tue 3.9%, Wed 5.5%, Thu 6.7%, Fri 2.5%. The config uses fallback 1.2 on Mon-Thu alike and 1.05 on Friday; the tuned Friday value equals Friday's measured miss price, while Monday and Thursday share one number although a Thursday miss costs 50% more and is late almost twice as often. Rough arithmetic with the model's fee slope: Monday at 1.12 opens about 0.02 lower, saves about 90 EUR on the 77 orders/wk that book at opening and costs about 57 on 5 more misses.
proposals.mechanism: The start model picks the fee that maximises chance x (fallback - fee); the fallback is what a miss costs. On Monday drivers are idle and a missed order still books near the lane value; on Thursday missed orders run into the Friday crunch and the weekend.
proposals.test: Config only: startFallbackDay [1.12, 1.2, 1.2, 1.28, 1.05], and separately [1.12, 1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 1.05] and [1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 1.28, 1.05] to see each end. Usual 40 and h1-h80. If proposal 1 is adopted, test a fallback by ready day instead (ready today 1.25, tomorrow 1.1, 2+ days 1.05).
proposals.confidence: Low. The miss costs by day are measured, but the net effect is a small difference of two larger numbers and startFallback 1.1 against 1.15 was flat in an earlier sweep (sm).
proposals.ontime_risk: Low: Monday orders open slightly lower (Monday misses are late 3.7% of the time), Thursday orders open higher, which helps the day with the highest late share.

found.nothing_found:
Lines that showed nothing worth a test:

- Holding an evening post for the morning: posts at 17:00-19:00 (69/wk) and 19:00-24:00 (12/wk) book at the opening fee as often as daytime posts (0.66 and 0.76 against 0.65), with the same late share and the same excess when they miss.
- Holding a Friday post: 19.5 Friday orders a week book on Friday at the opening fee (38% are even picked up that day) and the Saturday-morning cohort takes another 24. Holding would lose the Friday bookers.
- Posting a car that is ready in 2+ days only on the eve of its ready day: the handbook sentence is not a hard gate. 64%, 42% and 26% of first bookings for cars ready in 2, 3 and 4 days come on the post day, at 0.75-0.81 x lane, the cheapest bookings of all. Holding is worth at most about 80 EUR/wk on fee arithmetic and gives those up.
- Posting earlier: every order is already posted at the win; there is nothing earlier to move to.
- Orders booked within minutes at the opening fee: 91/wk book within 5 minutes (32% of opening-fee bookings, 2-5 viewers before the booking). The model's chance for them is the same as for slow bookings (0.71-0.72 against 0.73) and their opening fee is no higher. Slices with many instant bookings (Monday posts ready today: 42% within 5 minutes; delivery towns with 150+ drivers: 32%) are well calibrated (0.71 said, 0.74 actual). Saved weeks cannot show whether the fee slope is flatter there, because the opening fee is a fixed function of the features; that needs random opening fees (exploreFee) on such a slice.
- The lowest openers (at or under 0.65 x lane, 11.6/wk): the model overstates them (0.84-0.88 said, 0.45-0.71 actual), but they end at 0.72-0.74 x lane with under 1% late. No gain from raising startMin.
- Viewer counts: a missed order has a median of 72 distinct viewers before its first booking and 49% of bookers first see the gig within 10 minutes of booking. The count does not tell when a raise is needed.
- Offers: only 5% of first bookings above the opening fee come through an accepted offer.

Caveats. Proposals 2 and 3 share one mechanism and overlap; their gains do not add in full. data/results.log shows sweep sa reaching 18,306 on the usual 40 with feeCap 1.4, rampPow 1.5, feeSteps 16 and minAwake 240, above s7-k115 at 17,658, so the ramp proposals should be tested on that base too.

found.topic: Direct offers and driver behaviour (views, bookings, hold-outs) - 40 weeks of s7-k115 against 40 weeks of s9-off0 (offers off), 327,144 offers, 19,818 bookings, about 680,000 first views

proposals.title: Switch the fitted offer model on (it exists, the best config runs without it)
proposals.evidence: s7-k115 has offerModel null, so offers go by the point score. Measured on 40 weeks (8,179 offers, 21.5 accepted a week): 58% of all offers (4,706 a week) go to drivers who never viewed the order, live more than 30 km from the delivery and have not worked today; they return 1.25 accepts a week (1 in 3,760) and use 3,162 of the first or second daily offers. Offers to a driver who viewed the order in the last 30 minutes are taken 1.1-1.6% of the time (3.1% at 07-09 h) against 0.16% for never-viewed, yet only 393 a week are sent. An order has 9.6 viewers in its first 30 minutes and gets 2.5 offers then, of which 0.14 go to a viewer. 2,501 of 3,003 offered driver-days hit the 3-a-day limit (median third offer 14:36); 52% of viewers who did not book had no offers left when they looked. Earlier sweep on the older base gd-t3p3 (40 seeds): o2-m004 +146 +-108 with 3,199 offers and 26.7 accepts against 17.9; never re-run on the lane-anchored config.
proposals.mechanism: An accepted offer books a driver at today's fee who would otherwise wait for the ramp: accepted offers sit at fee/opening 1.117 while app orders still open at the same age end 0.18 higher, about EUR 8.6 saved per accept (185 a week), which with slightly earlier bookings is the whole EUR 330. The model spends the scarce resources (3 offers per driver per day, 3 open per gig) on recent viewers and on drivers living at the delivery end instead of on strangers.
proposals.test: Config only, on top of s7-k115 (usual 40) and s8-l35-u (h1..h80): offerModel = the weights of variant o2-m004 in bot/sweeps/o2.json (one -5.992, deAt 1.637, de30 1.434, de80 0.6, pu30 -0.284, here -0.184, worked 0.958, seen 0.101, long -1.181, fee -1.442, today -0.437, view30 2.303, view120 1.991, view600 1.255, viewOld -0.559, hour -1.593, evening -0.442, lnDone 0.387), offerMin 0.004. Second arm offerMin 0.003. Do not retest offerAge 60 (-238 against the model) or offerMin 0.008/0.015.
proposals.confidence: medium-low: mechanism measured clearly on current data, but the only direct test was 1.35 sigma on an older base
proposals.ontime_risk: neutral: 97.4% against 97.5% in the earlier sweep, lowest week 93.6%

proposals.title: Offer next-day pickups from the minute they are posted (replace the 20-hour cut-off)
proposals.evidence: No offer is ever sent for a car ready more than 20 hours ahead (0 of 327,144). Just inside the limit, offers for cars ready in 14-20 h are taken 0.40% of the time (6.1 accepts a week from 1,539 offers) against 0.22% for cars ready now; pickups not today 0.385% against 0.228% today. Offers in an order's first 30 minutes on the board are taken 0.59-0.66% against 0.13-0.27% at 1-10 hours, and delaying the first offer by 60 minutes cost 238 in the o2 sweep. Of the 88 driver-order pairs a week that viewed at a lower fee and booked later at a higher one (raises paid EUR 1,157 a week, 13.3 each, first seen at 0.877 lane, booked at 1.058), 30% (26 a week, EUR 279 of raises) first looked while the pickup was more than 20 h away, so they could not be offered; 25.5% of all non-booking first views are in that state.
proposals.mechanism: Most views come in the first minutes after posting. For an order won in the morning for tomorrow morning, the cut-off blocks offers for hours, until those viewers are gone and the hour of day is worse (viewer offers: 3.1% at 07-09, 1.7% at 09-12, 0.7% at 12-15). Most drivers know whether they work tomorrow, so they can accept.
proposals.test: desk.ts, the line `if (first > this.now + 20 * HOUR) continue` in sendModelOffers (about line 1551) and in sendOffers (about line 1611): replace with `if (Math.floor(first / DAY) > today + 1) continue`, or add a Config field offerAhead (hours, default 20) and test 30 and 44. Test with and without proposal 1.
proposals.confidence: low-medium: acceptance beyond 20 h is extrapolated from the 14-20 h band
proposals.ontime_risk: none expected; earlier bookings of next-day cars if anything help

proposals.title: Refit the offer model on current weeks in lane units, with second-look and raised-fee terms
proposals.evidence: 40 weeks of s7-k115: offer within 30 min of a driver's second or later view of the order: 3.4% accepted (10.4% of read offers) against 1.1% after a first view; viewer offers when the fee has already risen above the opening fee 1.66% against 0.85% at the opening fee; hour slope is much steeper for viewers (3.1% at 07-09 to 0.29% at 15-18) than for strangers (0.17% to 0.13%). The point score's +5 for a driver who just delivered within 40 km of the pickup is not supported: 0.9% accepted, same as any driver who worked today (read 53-62%, accepted when read 1.7%); a view older than 10 hours is worth nothing (0.27%). Among drivers who viewed, were offered afterwards and took the gig one way or the other, about 42% took it through the offer (10.5 accepted against 4.4 declined-then-booked-higher and 7.8 unread-then-booked-higher a week).
proposals.mechanism: A second look is a driver who is waiting for the raise; the offer removes the reason to wait. The current model was fitted on x-booked110 weeks with fee over the noisy typical fee and has one hour slope for everybody.
proposals.test: tools/offers5.py with `fit` on s7-k115 weeks, fee divided by the lane value from bot/lanes.json instead of p['ref'], plus features view2 (driver has 2 or more views of the order), raised (fee now above the fee at the driver's first view), viewHour (view30 or view120 times (hour-7)/10). In desk.ts keep per order and driver the view count and first-seen fee beside the last view time (the viewers map filled at about lines 551-552), add the three terms in sendModelOffers (about lines 1554-1583) and divide the fee by the lane value there. Compare against proposal 1 as base.
proposals.confidence: low: large effects per offer but on small counts (37 second-look offers a week); overlaps proposal 1

proposals.title: Price with a wider win curve than the one the model learns with (new market.quoteScale)
proposals.evidence: The bot's own win forecast is too steep. On the 12,281 quotes with one option asked and one priced (40 weeks), won ~ a + b x logit(bot p) gives b = 0.865 (0.882 on calm hours only), a = +0.14. By bin of bot p -> share won: 0.05 -> 0.074, 0.22 -> 0.289, 0.37 -> 0.457, 0.53 -> 0.546, 0.67 -> 0.677, 0.79 -> 0.773. So above the flip point the bot wins 7 to 9 points more often than it expects; below it the forecast is right. Mean width of the bot's curve is 0.081 in log price (scale 0.07 plus belief variance); a pooled model that knows each world's day level, dealer and places still needs 0.105. Re-pricing every quote with the bot's own belief and own cost but a curve k times as wide, valued by the pooled model: k=1.15: +113 EUR/wk (+80 without each world's outage day), wins -16/wk, price +1.0%; k=1.3: +186 (+126), wins -34, price +2.2%; k=1.5: +204 (+124), wins -60; k=0.85: -146. The gain sits where bot p < 0.6 (k=1.3: +58 for p<0.35, +90 for 0.35-0.6, +39 above) and late in the week (Thu-Fri +96, Mon +19). Counter-evidence that keeps my estimate below the model's: real runs so far punished dearer quotes made through cost (feeK 1.20 vs 1.15: -38 on the 40 usual seeds, -114 on 80 fresh; feeK 1.10: +126 / +75), and market.scale 0.08, which widens pricing and slows learning together, lost 163 (mk2-sc8).
proposals.mechanism: market.scale does two jobs: it sets how fast a win or loss moves the belief, and how fast the win chance falls with price in the optimiser. Sweeps picked a narrow value because narrow learns faster, but the narrow curve makes the optimiser think a high quote almost never wins, so it shades cost-heavy quotes (backlog, long lanes, Thursday and Friday) down towards the flip point. Splitting the two keeps the fast learning and prices on the calibrated curve.

proposals.evidence: From data/results.log, every paired 40-week comparison of a narrower scale against a wider one on older configs favours the narrower: mk-full-sc7 +136 and mk-full-sc6 +379 (t=4.3) against mk-full; mk2-sc6 +36 and mk2-sc8 -163 against mk2-a; mk3-sc6 +26 and mk3-sc65 +52 against mk3-a; sk-64-sc65 +152 (t=1.6) against sk-64. proposals.title: Re-anchor the fee on the new lane when a dealer changes the destination of an order that still has no driver
proposals.evidence: 40 weeks of s7-k115. Place changes: 9.4 a week, of which 2.3 a week hit an order still waiting for a driver. After the change the desk withdraws the gig and posts it again, but the new gig opens at 0.87-0.88 x the OLD lane's typical fee in every group. (a) New lane more than 13% cheaper: 43 orders (1.07/wk), new lane is 0.48 x the old on average; the repost opens at 2.36 x the NEW lane's typical fee and books within a median 0.5 h at 2.40 x (EUR 100 paid where 0.9 x the new lane is EUR 44). Overpayment against 0.9 x new lane: EUR 60 a week. (b) New lane more than 15% dearer: 32 orders (0.80/wk), new lane 2.84 x the old; the repost opens at 0.39 x the new lane, the top of its whole schedule is 0.73 x, it books at 0.79 x after a median 39 h while the last on-time pickup was a median 25 h away: 69% late (22 of 32), margin EUR -46.8 an order, refunds EUR 22.5 a week. Changes within 15% (0.42/wk): 6% late, no problem. For comparison all orders: 2.2% late.
proposals.mechanism: onChanged() stores the new order but schedule() computes its reference from refOf(ord.request, ...), and ord.request still holds the old pickup and delivery places and the old referenceFeeCents. ord.shownFee (highest fee shown so far) also keeps the opening at the old level, so a much shorter trip is posted at the long trip's fee, and a much longer trip starts and caps far below what any driver takes until the urgent ramp (which is also a multiple of the old reference) runs out of time.
proposals.test: Code change in C:\Users\trevo\spread\bot\desk.ts, onChanged(order) (about line 1016), before the open gigs are withdrawn: if any leg's pickup or delivery placeId differs from ord.request.legs[i], compute ratio = lanes[newPickup>newDelivery] / lanes[oldPickup>oldDelivery] from lanesOf(cfg.lanesFile) (fall back to the ratio of roadMinutes when a lane is missing); replace ord.request by a copy with the new places in its legs and referenceFeeCents multiplied by ratio (a copy, so the market model's stored request is untouched); multiply ord.shownFee by ratio; set ord.startMult = null and ord.climb = null. refOf() (line 700) reads request.legs[0], so the existing withdraw-and-repost then draws opening fee, ramp cap and urgent ramp from the new lane. Judge on the affected orders, not the weekly mean (about 1.9 orders a week, effect below the noise of a 40-week mean): fee at booking over the new lane's value on cheaper lanes (target about 0.9-1.0 instead of 2.40) and late share on dearer lanes (target under 25% instead of 69%).
proposals.confidence: High for the mechanism (code and data agree: both groups reopen at 0.87-0.88 x the old lane); medium for the size (75 affected orders in 40 weeks). About EUR 60 a week from the cheaper lanes, roughly break-even in cash on the dearer lanes (EUR 11 more fees, up to EUR 22 fewer refunds) plus the trust those dealers keep.
